intro: ばかり pictures one thing filling all the space. After a noun or a て-form it means "nothing but, all the time", usually with a note of excess or complaint. After a た-form it means the action has only just happened: so recent that it still fills the speaker's present.

skills.rule: X ばかり means "nothing but X, X all the time", usually as too much; ～てばかりいる means "do nothing but ~".
skills.explain:
Noun + ばかり says one thing takes up everything, again and again or in large numbers: 甘い物ばかり食べる (eats nothing but sweets), 最近は雨ばかりです (nothing but rain lately), 女性ばかりのクラス (a class of all women). It usually sounds critical or surprised. Casual speech says ばっかり.

With a verb, use the て-form + ばかりいる: 寝てばかりいる (does nothing but sleep), 文句を言ってばかりいる. As a request, ～てばかりいないで means "stop just ~ing".

The edge with だけ: だけ is a neutral, exclusive limit and works for a single item (一人だけ); ばかり needs repetition or a crowd, so it cannot mean "only one". が and を never come before ばかり: they are left out or follow it (肉ばかりを食べる); other particles usually come before it (友達とばかり遊ぶ). Number + ばかり meaning "about" (十日ばかり) is literary; in conversation use ぐらい.
patterns: [noun] ばかりだ / ばかりの [noun]  "all, full of"
[verb て-form] ばかりいる  "do nothing but"

examples.jp: 弟[おとうと]はゲーム{ばかり}しています。
examples.en: My younger brother does nothing but play games.

examples.jp: 最近[さいきん]は雨[あめ]{ばかり}ですね。
examples.en: It's been nothing but rain lately, hasn't it?

examples.jp: 甘[あま]い物[もの]{ばかり}食[た]べないでください。
examples.en: Please don't eat sweet things all the time.

examples.jp: このクラスは女性[じょせい]{ばかり}です。
姉[あね]は文句[もんく]を言[い]って{ばかり}います。
examples.en: My older sister does nothing but complain.

examples.jp: 寝[ね]て{ばかり}いないで、少[すこ]し手伝[てつだ]って。
examples.en: Stop just lying around and help a bit.

contrast.note: だけ states an exclusive limit, neutrally, and can apply to one thing: 野菜だけ食べる (eats only vegetables). ばかり says that is all you ever see, often as a complaint: 野菜ばかり食べる (eats vegetables all the time).
しか needs a negative verb and means "no more than": 野菜しか食べない. ばかり takes a positive verb.

mistakes.bad: 毎日[まいにち]テレビを見[み]る{ばかり}います。
mistakes.good: 毎日[まいにち]テレビを見[み]て{ばかり}います。
mistakes.note: "Do nothing but" is the て-form + ばかりいる.

mistakes.bad: 会議[かいぎ]には一人[ひとり]{ばかり}来[き]ました。
mistakes.good: 会議[かいぎ]には一人[ひとり]{だけ}来[き]ました。
mistakes.note: A single person is a limit, not a crowd or a repetition: "only one" is だけ.

skills.tip: "All the time, too much" and you sound a bit annoyed: ばかり. A plain "only this": だけ.

skills.rule: Verb た-form + ばかり means "have just done", by the speaker's feeling; it acts like a noun, so it takes です, の + noun, なのに or なので.
skills.explain:
～たばかり says the action is so recent that it still shapes the present: 今起きたばかりです (I've just woken up), 日本に来たばかりなので、まだ分かりません. The recency is the speaker's feeling, so it can stretch: 先月入社したばかり, 去年買ったばかりなのに壊れた.

Grammatically the phrase works like a noun: ～たばかりです, ～たばかりの + noun (買ったばかりの傘), ～たばかりなのに (even though I only just), ～たばかりなので / だから. It needs the た-form; a dictionary form + ばかり does not mean "just did".

The neighbour is ところ. ～たところ marks the exact moment just after the action, measured objectively: 今着いたところです. Both work for "a moment ago", but with a past time word like 先月 or 去年 only ばかり works. Note also 食べただけ, which means "I only ate" (and did nothing else), not "just ate".
patterns: [verb た-form] ばかりです  "have just done"
[verb た-form] ばかりなのに / なので

examples.jp: 今[いま]起[お]きた{ばかり}です。
買[か]った{ばかり}の傘[かさ]をなくしました。
examples.en: I lost the umbrella I had just bought.

examples.jp: 先月[せんげつ]入社[にゅうしゃ]した{ばかり}です。
examples.en: I only joined the company last month.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に来[き]た{ばかり}なので、まだ何[なに]も分[わ]かりません。
examples.en: I've only just come to Japan, so I don't know anything yet.

examples.jp: さっき食[た]べた{ばかり}なのに、もうお腹[なか]が空[す]きました。
examples.en: I only just ate, but I'm already hungry.

contrast.note: ～たところ is the objective moment just after: 今帰ったところです. ～たばかり is subjective recency and can cover weeks or years: 去年結婚したばかりです. Dictionary form + ところ means "about to" (今出るところ).
～ただけ limits the action: 見ただけです (I only looked, I didn't buy). ～たばかり places it in time: 見たばかりです (I've just seen it).

mistakes.bad: 去年[きょねん]結婚[けっこん]した{ところ}です。
mistakes.good: 去年[きょねん]結婚[けっこん]した{ばかり}です。
mistakes.note: With a past time word like 去年, "just" is the speaker's feeling of recency: ばかり, not ところ.

mistakes.bad: 買[か]った{ばかり}靴[くつ]が汚[よご]れました。
mistakes.good: 買[か]った{ばかり}の靴[くつ]が汚[よご]れました。
mistakes.note: Before a noun, ～たばかり needs の.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]に着[つ]く{ばかり}です。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]に着[つ]いた{ばかり}です。

skills.tip: た-form before the blank and English says "just": ばかり. A time word like 先月 or 去年 in the sentence rules out ところ.
